question: A portable CMS designer proposes 'DLY' to mean DELAY. Using Section 1D.08 and Table 1D-3, is this acceptable and why?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No, "DLY" is not acceptable. Table 1D-3 lists DLY as an unacceptable abbreviation because, although intended to mean "Delay," it is commonly misinterpreted as "Daily." Section 1D.08 makes the prohibition mandatory, and Section 2L.05 requires all CMS abbreviations to comply with Section 1D.08. Standards (mandatory): - "The abbreviations shown in Table 1D-3 shall not be used in connection with traffic control devices because of their potential to be misinterpreted by road users." - "Abbreviations displayed on CMS shall comply with the provisions of Section 1D.08." - "When the word messages shown in Table 1D-2 need to be abbreviated on a portable changeable message sign, the abbreviations shown in Table 1D-2 shall be used." (DLY is not among the abbreviations shown in Table 1D-2, so it may not be substituted.) Visual evidence: - [Image 2] shows Table 1D-3 (Unacceptable Abbreviations) listing "DLY" with intended word "Delay" and common misinterpretation "Daily." - [Image 1] shows Table 1D-2 (Sheet 1 of 2) with the approved abbreviations for portable CMS messages; no abbreviation for "Delay" is provided. - [Image 3] shows Table 1D-1 (Acceptable Abbreviations), which likewise contains no approved abbreviation for "Delay." Citations: - Section 1D.08 Standard §4 (p.34) - Section 2L.05 Standard §6 (p.516) - Section 1D.08 Standard §2 (p.34) - Table 1D-3 (p.37) - Table 1D-2 (p.36) - Table 1D-1 (p.35)
gold_answer: No. DLY is explicitly prohibited because it can be misinterpreted as DAILY.
